subject.title: [Bug]: Control UI header logo/icon not displaying after 2026.3.24 update

question: Should root-mounted Control UI support hard refreshes/bookmarks on legacy or arbitrary prefixed routes such as /connections/chat with public assets resolving, or should those paths be treated as unsupported and redirected/documented?
rationale: Current source shows a remaining route-prefixed asset behavior, but the correct fix depends on whether maintainers want to support legacy/non-tab URL prefixes or keep only documented root, known app routes, configured basePath, and /__openclaw__/ behavior.

options.title: Support safe legacy/deep routes
options.body: Land a narrow allowlist or redirect that makes known Control UI public assets resolve for supported legacy/deep routes without aliasing arbitrary static filenames.

options.title: Limit to documented entrypoints
options.body: Document or enforce root/configured-basePath entrypoints and close the stale linked fork work as unsupported for arbitrary prefixes.

options.title: Adopt or replace the fork PR
options.body: Use the open fork PR only if its approach matches the chosen URL contract; otherwise request or queue a fresh narrow replacement after the decision.

recommendation.title: Support safe legacy/deep routes
recommendation.body: Land a narrow allowlist or redirect that makes known Control UI public assets resolve for supported legacy/deep routes without aliasing arbitrary static filenames.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on gateway Control UI public-asset routing and are best placed to decide the URL-contract boundary.
